thesis: Corcept reported Q2 2026 product revenue of $256.15M, up 32% year over year, with net income of $42.14M and diluted EPS of $0.36, and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.1-1.2B. The newly launched ovarian-cancer therapy LIFYORLI (relacorilant) contributed $47.6M in its first quarter of availability, with more than 1,300 patients treated, over 1,000 prescribing physicians and coverage policies for more than 70% of relevant insured lives. The stock is up 37.7% over the trailing 60 days and sits 6.4% below its 52-week high. The strongest counter-case is that this is a stock at an all-time high on a stretched valuation, with analyst ratings spanning Strong Buy to Strong Sell, carrying an unresolved binary event: the FDA has set a December 17, 2026 action date on the resubmitted relacorilant application for Cushing's syndrome. That does not change the read here, because the quarter and the raise rest on already-launched, already-reimbursed LIFYORLI and Korlym revenue rather than on the pending Cushing's decision — the disclosed revenue base and the guidance raise stand whatever December brings, and an approval would be additive rather than load-bearing.
invalidation: quarterly product revenue growth falls off the raised $1.1-1.2B full-year guidance path, LIFYORLI's sequential contribution stalls, or 2026 guidance is walked back

thesis: SpaceX's first earnings report since its June IPO, on August 4, beat on both lines: revenue of $7.81B against $6.93B expected and a loss of $0.09 per share against $0.26 expected, with Connectivity contributing $4.3B of revenue and 1.7M net subscriber adds and AI segment revenue up 247% year over year to $2.6B. The stock nonetheless fell about 8% in extended trading, is down 27.3% over the trailing 60 days, and is roughly 29% below its June IPO level. The offsetting disclosure is capital intensity: first-half capital expenditure of $28.5B, more than four times the year-ago level and more than twice quarterly revenue, with management expecting that pace to stay elevated. Reporting also notes that much of the AI revenue sits in a small number of contracts terminable on 90 days' notice, that Starlink is carrying losses in both the Space and AI segments, and that a 911-million-share lockup expiry landed days after the print. This suggests a company growing fast while outspending its own revenue by a wide margin. The beat and the spending-plus-supply overhang point in opposite directions and this run's research does not resolve which dominates, so the evidence is mixed rather than net-positive.
invalidation: capital expenditure growth decelerates toward operating cash generation, or the post-lockup share supply is absorbed without further price deterioration — either would make the read constructive rather than unresolved

thesis: Rocket Lab's Q2 2026 report carried record revenue of $234.07M, up 62% year over year and above the $230.94M consensus, with product revenue nearly doubling to $181.35M, backlog of $2.36B (up 137% year over year), and Q3 2026 guidance of $250-265M against an analyst estimate near $235.9M. Against that, the net loss of $0.08 per share was wider than the $0.06 consensus, though narrower than the $0.13 loss a year earlier, and CEO Peter Beck said the window to fly Neutron before the end of 2026 is narrowing as testing continues. The stock fell about 8% on the report and is down 26.5% over the trailing 60 days, now 47% below its 52-week high. The counter-case to holding a long is exactly that: Neutron slipping into 2027 removes the growth catalyst investors have been paying for, and this run cannot settle that execution risk against the record backlog and above-consensus guidance. This suggests a launch and space-systems business growing strongly on disclosed numbers while carrying an unresolved schedule risk on its largest single catalyst.
invalidation: Neutron's first flight is formally pushed beyond 2026, Q3 revenue lands below the $250M guidance floor, or backlog stops growing

thesis: LYTE is the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF, which began trading on Cboe BZX on August 6, 2026 at $25.73 with $72M of first-day volume — seven daily bars of history in total. It is a 12-position thematic fund charging 0.65%, holding at least 80% of net assets in companies deriving 50% or more of revenue from optical transceivers and modules, laser sources, silicon photonics integrated circuits, optical interconnect systems or photonic wafer materials; disclosed top holdings are Lumentum (15.42%), Coherent (15.23%), NewLink (14.59%), ZTE (14.22%) and Tianfu Communication (7.9%). The screen flagged it only because its price sits 1.25% below its '52-week' high, but with seven sessions in existence that extreme is a seven-day high, so the signal is a mechanical artifact of a new listing rather than evidence about the fund. There is no company-disclosed catalyst to read for a fund, and the plausible positive — that the AI-optical spending cycle lifting its holdings is real and durable — cannot be resolved into a view on this particular wrapper, whose concentration puts roughly 28% into two China-listed optical names.
invalidation: enough trading history accumulates for the 52-week extreme test to carry information, at which point re-screen on the fund's own record rather than on a seven-day range

thesis: Sandisk is down 22.1% over the trailing 60 days and 29.5% below its 52-week high, having fallen roughly 56% from a June 25 closing high of $2,335.00 to $1,015.89 on July 29 — the S&P 500's worst performer for the month, down about 47% in July — then rebounding 25.99% in a single session on July 30. Reporting attributes the collapse to a broad memory and AI-infrastructure de-rating on fears that hyperscalers are overspending on capital expenditure, to Chinese AI-model and IPO headlines feared to pressure component pricing, and to forced flows from a leveraged fund, with one account stating the July collapse 'had little to do with Sandisk's fundamentals and a lot to do with one leveraged fund.' Weak earnings guidance is also cited as a driver, but this run did not read the guidance figures in any source and so treats that print as unconfirmed rather than supplying a number. The plausible positive — that a 56%-down-then-26%-up tape marks capitulation in a structurally tight NAND market — is precisely what mechanical, sector-driven price action cannot settle, so this move is not readable as a company-specific fundamental signal.
invalidation: Sandisk discloses quarterly results and forward guidance that can be read directly, replacing sector flow as the explanation for the price

thesis: AST SpaceMobile is down 18.9% over the trailing 60 days and 47% below its 52-week high on a chain of specific, already-disclosed company negatives. Q2 2026, reported August 10, showed revenue of $31.5M against a $35.18M consensus and an adjusted loss of $0.77 per share against $0.26 expected; Q1 2026 had already missed at $14.7M revenue against a $38.4M consensus with a $0.66 loss against $0.23 expected. On July 15-16 the company announced and priced a $1B convertible senior notes offering, and shares fell 17% on July 16 on the heaviest trading volume of the month. Separately, an SEC filing disclosed that roughly 45 BlueBird satellites are now expected in orbit in early 2027 against prior guidance of end-2026 — an admission the constellation is behind schedule. The strongest positive counter-case is that the convertible removes near-term funding risk and the constellation still gets built. That does not change the read, because the same disclosure cycle that supplied the cash also pushed the revenue ramp out by roughly half a year: the financing extends runway toward a later ramp rather than accelerating it, and does so by adding convertible dilution on top of a revenue line still missing consensus by wide margins.
invalidation: the company discloses a deployment cadence that recovers the end-2026 satellite target, or quarterly revenue converges on consensus rather than missing it by half

thesis: Cerebras' second post-IPO report, on August 12, cut both ways and its two headline metrics point in opposite directions, so both are quoted: core revenue of $180M missed the $194M analysts expected, while the company raised its full-year revenue forecast and posted a smaller-than-expected adjusted loss. Bloomberg reported that the hardware business declined, which management framed as 'lumpy' demand, and CEO Andrew Feldman said AI demand is 'through the roof' with customers paying up for its inference chips. The stock fell 11.8% on August 13 and a further 5.2% on August 14 on 2.44x its 30-day average volume — the spike that flagged this candidate — leaving it 43% below its 52-week high. An earlier account attributing the drop to 'reports of weakening AI chip demand' is contradicted by the company's own commentary and by the raised forecast, so that explanation is discarded rather than carried. What remains is a revenue miss and a shrinking hardware line set against a raised outlook and a narrower loss; this run engaged that conflict directly and could not settle which one the market is pricing.
invalidation: Q3 revenue converges on the raised full-year path and the hardware line returns to growth, or the raised full-year forecast is walked back — either resolves the conflict this thesis could not

thesis: Corning's Q2 2026 report on July 28 beat on both lines — core EPS of $0.78 against $0.75 expected on core sales of $4.74B against $4.63B — with Optical Communications sales up 32% to $2.07B including a 65% increase in Enterprise Networks, two newly announced hyperscaler agreements described as comparable in scale to its earlier multiyear Meta deal, and the Springboard plan extended to a $40B annualized run rate by 2030. The stock nonetheless fell about 18% that day, its largest single-day decline since July 2002, and roughly 46% over July. The disclosed drags are a Q3 core sales guide of $4.9-5.0B against a consensus near $5.0B, and management's expectation that global handheld-device shipments decline by a mid-teens percentage in 2026 as high memory prices raise handset costs and weaken consumer demand. The counter-case to a long is that this consumer and display drag offsets the AI-optical growth in aggregate; this run read no figure that settles that netting, and part of the drawdown is a sector-wide unwind that also hit Lumentum, Coherent, Marvell and AXT rather than anything Corning disclosed. This suggests the optical growth engine is intact at 38.9% below the 52-week high, with the size of the offset unquantified.
invalidation: Optical Communications growth decelerates out of the 30%-plus range, or a further guidance cut extends the shortfall beyond the handheld-device line into the AI-driven segments

thesis: Micron is down 10.7% over the trailing 60 days and 22.5% below its 52-week high, and the decline this run can source is sector-wide rather than company-specific: a broad semiconductor and AI-infrastructure selloff that hit Western Digital, Applied Materials, Marvell, AMD and Nvidia alongside Micron, driven by AI-valuation concerns, weak sentiment following Samsung's preliminary results, and DeepSeek-related headlines, together with buyer pushback against memory pricing. No Micron-disclosed event inside the window explains the move. Reporting cites a fiscal fourth-quarter outlook of roughly 20.6% sequential revenue growth with gross margin near 86%, and Citigroup cutting its price target 18% to $1,150 while keeping a Buy and pointing to multi-year pricing contracts — but this run did not read those figures in a company source and treats them as unconfirmed rather than as a disclosed print. The plausible positive, that contracted pricing insulates Micron from the spot-market pushback dragging the group lower, is precisely the claim this run could not verify, so a macro-driven drawdown does not constitute a company-specific entry signal.
invalidation: Micron reports fiscal Q4 results and guidance that can be read directly against the pricing-pushback concern, replacing sector rotation as the explanation for the move

thesis: Astera Labs, currently held, reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $392.4M on August 4, up 104% year over year, beating on both revenue and earnings, and guided fiscal Q3 to $540-560M — roughly 40% sequential growth at the midpoint and above analyst expectations. The stock rose 12.7% on the print, then fell about 12% the following session, and is down 17.4% over the trailing 60 days at 35.5% below its 52-week high. Reporting attributes that reversal to positioning rather than to the results: shares had risen four sessions running into the report, including 20.0% on July 30, so the drop reads as profit-taking after a pre-earnings rally rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration. That framing is also why this cannot be rated higher — explaining an adverse move as mechanical is a judgement about flows, not about the business, and a targeted re-search found no litigation, financing, or leadership disclosure that would supply a fundamental explanation instead. The disclosed results and the above-consensus Q3 guide continue to support holding the position.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the $540M guidance floor, or the product ramp underpinning the ~40% sequential step-up slips

thesis: Coherent, currently held, reported fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results on August 12-13 with Q4 revenue of $2.05B and full-year revenue of $7.118B, up 22.5%. The two profitability measures diverge and both are reported here: on a GAAP basis, gross margin of 38.5% and net income of $1.19 per diluted share; on a non-GAAP basis, gross margin of 40.2% and net income of $1.74 per diluted share. Guidance for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 is revenue of $2.2-2.4B with non-GAAP gross margin of 39.5-41.5% and non-GAAP EPS of $1.85-2.05 — a sequential step up from the quarter just reported — and coverage described the print as exceeding Wall Street expectations. The stock nonetheless fell about 8% on August 13 and is down 21.3% over the trailing 60 days, 25.9% below its 52-week high. That reaction is the counter-case and this run could not settle it: the whole optical complex has been de-rating since Corning's July 28 guidance, and nothing in Coherent's own disclosures read this run accounts for an 8% decline on a beat accompanied by a higher guide. The results support continuing to hold; the market's response to them remains unexplained.
invalidation: Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue lands below the $2.2B guidance floor, or datacom and AI optical demand commentary turns negative
sources: Coherent Q4 and FY2026 press release: https://www.coherent.com/news/press-releases/fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-results

thesis: Dell, currently held, is up 20.0% over the trailing 60 days and trades 4.5% below its 52-week high, closing at $484.50 on August 12 after a 9.87% single-session gain. Two distinct things drive that and this run cannot rank one as clearly dominant. The company-specific piece: reporting cites fiscal Q1 revenue up 88% with AI-optimized server revenue of $16.1B (up 757%) and an AI server backlog of $51.3B, a raised FY2027 AI-server goal of $60B from a prior $50B, a total FY2027 revenue goal of $165-169B, and an AI cloud startup, Volta, emerging from stealth with a $10B partnership naming Dell as technology provider for a 133MW facility in Norway. The sector piece: the August 12 move itself was attributed to strong results from CoreWeave and Super Micro lifting the entire hardware complex — a read-through from peers, not a Dell disclosure. The counter-case is margin: AI servers carry thinner margins than Dell's traditional mix, and this run read revenue, backlog and target figures but no gross-margin figure that would settle whether that volume converts to profit. Support for holding rests on disclosed backlog and targets, with the profitability question left open.
invalidation: AI-server gross margin is disclosed at a level that makes the backlog uneconomic, or the raised FY2027 AI-server goal is reduced

thesis: Microsoft, currently held, is up 23.9% over the trailing 60 days, driven by a roughly 19% three-session surge from a pre-earnings base in the $390s on July 29 to $451.10 on July 30 and $464.72 on July 31 following its earnings report, and now trades 10.1% below its 52-week high. This run's research confirms the timing and size of that earnings-driven move but did not surface the reported revenue or EPS figures in any source, so the print is unconfirmed here and is deliberately not described as a beat, a miss, or a raise. Against it, Microsoft faces a securities class action alleging that it made materially misleading statements about its AI initiatives and Azure cloud business during 2025 and early 2026, specifically that its public statements painted a misleading picture of Copilot's success and AI investment returns. The lead-plaintiff deadline was August 11, 2026 and has passed, and this run found no scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline within the next ~90 days, so the matter is noted in this narrative rather than flagged in risk_flags. That counter-case was engaged and could not be settled: the allegations go to the durability of the same AI and Azure narrative that produced the move, and neither their merits nor the quarter's actual figures were verified this run. The position is supported by disclosed price action and the absence of a scheduled adverse legal step, not by verified fundamentals.
invalidation: a court sets a ruling or trial date in the securities class action, or Azure and Copilot growth figures disclosed next quarter fail to support the post-earnings re-rating
